summary: evals/subject seeding: know() now ensures the target peer exists in Honcho before writing a seeded conclusion about them, fixing a 404 that surfaced as 'could not write a conclusion ... Honcho did not accept it' against two live participation cases.
details: Root cause, confirmed live against a real Honcho instance: workspace_for() (nora/subject/obtain.py) hands every eval case a fresh, isolated Honcho workspace, so a target peer named only in a case's `knows.conclusions` has never been created there. Production never hits this because a peer always exists by the time anything concludes about it -- created by a real feed() call first.

Curled Honcho's /conclusions endpoint directly to isolate the failure from the SSH tunnel/latency theory first raised when the error appeared: same call against an existing production peer succeeded (201); against a never-created peer it 404'd ('Peer ... not found in workspace ...'), which is exactly the failure the eval's two participation cases hit.

Fix: nora/subject/knowledge.py's know() calls memory.ensure_peer(peer_id=...) before its conclude() loop -- ensure_peer is already part of the MemoryStore protocol (nora/domain/ports.py:754), unused by this call site until now.

tests/unit/test_subject_knowledge.py: two new tests. FakeMemory enforces the real Honcho invariant (conclude fails for an unensured peer) rather than a mock the fix could trivially satisfy without calling ensure_peer correctly. Falsified: removing the fix line reproduced the exact live RuntimeError message; restored, both pass.
